001.en: Which concept is illustrated when an employee is granted permission to the company’s new file-sharing platform for daily use?

006.en: “The service consumer gains access to the service provider’s resources and uses them according to the agreed terms and conditions.” In this case, the employee is granted permission to use the ‘resource’ of the file sharing platform. Ref 3.1.2

007.en: An IT support engineer assisting a user in configuring their laptop is an example of which concept?

011.en: Service actions are actions “performed by a service provider or jointly by a service provider and a service consumer. Fulfilment of service requests is a common form of service actions. Other examples include delivery of goods, user training, consultations, and so on.” In this case, the service provider team has taken an action by assisting the user. Ref 3.1.2

012.en: What influences whether a service is perceived as valuable by a consumer?

013.en: The service provider’s ability to minimize their operational costs

014.en: The number of providers delivering the service to the consumer

015.en: The extent to which the positive effects of the service outweigh the negative ones

016.en: The amount of money the service provider invests in resources

017.en: Services can introduce new costs and risks, and in some cases, they can negatively affect some of the intended outcomes, while supporting others. Services are valuable when the positive effects outweigh the negative ones. Ref 3.1.1

018.en: Which of the following is TRUE regarding services and desired outcomes?

019.en: Services guarantee that all intended outcomes will be achieved

020.en: Services completely eliminate risks associated with achieving outcomes

021.en: Services always result in positive effects without exceptions

022.en: Services may have unintended and surprising outcomes, both positive and negative

023.en: When enabling desired outcomes for service consumers, services may also prevent or reduce other desired outcomes or introduce undesired ones […] In addition to the intended and anticipated positive and negative effect on service consumers, services may have unintended and surprising outcomes, both positive and negative. Ref 3.1.1

024.en: A service provider commits to using recyclable components, reducing carbon emissions, and maintaining transparent supply chains. Which concept does this commitment represent?

026.en: “Sustainability requirements may include responsible sourcing of materials and components, responsible work and employment practices, use of clean energy, low carbon footprint, incorporation of recycled and recyclable materials, transparent supply chains, and others. These requirements may originate from national and international regulations and standards or be defined in the organization’s sustainability strategy.” Ref 3.2.4

027.en: Which dimension of product and service management is directly influenced by leadership commitment to psychological safety and continual learning?

032.en: The ‘Organization and people’ dimension is most concerned with establishing a culture of trust. Digitally enabled organizations are under pressure to continually improve their performance under changing market conditions […] The challenge for these organizations is to foster an effective set of shared beliefs, perceptions, and values in relation to risks. This, in turn, should create a safety culture, and result in behavior that is beneficial for all stakeholders, including the members of the organization. Ref 2.2.1

033.en: Which of the following dimension of product and service management addresses organizational and cross-organizational workflows?

034.en: “The ‘Value streams and processes’ dimension address organizational and cross-organizational workflows, focusing on what activities the organization undertakes and how they are organized to enable value for stakeholders effectively and eficiently.” Ref 2.3

035.en: Which dimension of product and service management addresses data and technologies used in digital product and services?

036.en: “The ‘Information and technology’ dimension addresses data, information, and technologies used in digital products and services, as well as those used as part of the organization’s product and service management systems.” Ref 2.4

037.en: Which dimension of product and service management is concerned with relationships with other organizations that are involved in discovery, design and continual improvement of product?

038.en: “The ‘Partners and suppliers’ dimension encompasses an organization’s relationships with other organizations that are involved in the discovery, design, build, transition, operation, delivery, support, and/or continual improvement of products and services.” Ref 2.5

039.en: According to the ‘Focus on value’ ITIL Guiding Principle, all organizational activities should link back to what?

040.en: Benefits for organization, its customers, and stakeholders

044.en: The ‘Focus on value’ principle stipulates that all “activities conducted by the organization should link back, directly or indirectly, to value for itself, its customers, and other stakeholders.” Ref 5.2.1

045.en: According to the ITIL Guiding Principle ‘Start where you are’, what is the MAIN risk of starting over without considering what is already available when improving a service?

046.en: Losing opportunities for collaboration and shared understanding across teams

047.en: Overcomplicating solutions by ignoring practical, simple approaches

048.en: Failing to gather feedback needed to guide gradual improvement

049.en: Wasting time and losing valuable existing capabilities and resources

050.en: When improving products or services, starting over completely is rarely wise. The approach of completely removing what has been done “can be extremely wasteful, not only in terms of time, but also in terms of the loss of existing capabilities, competencies, people, and tools that could have significant value in the improvement effort. Do not start over without first considering what is already available to be leveraged.” Ref 5.2.2

051.en: What is the MAIN purpose of using feedback throughout improvement iterations?

052.en: To confirm that all stakeholder opinions are in agreement

053.en: To ensure that improvement actions remain relevant and effective in changing circumstances

054.en: To prevent the need for further adjustments once work has started

055.en: To avoid changes in project priorities during implementation

056.en: Faster response to customer needs is one of the benefits of embedding feedback loops. “Working in a timeboxed, iterative manner with feedback loops embedded into the workflow allows for […] faster responses to customer and business needs” Ref 5.2.3.2

057.en: A design team is creating a new workflow and tries to account for every possible exception. What is the consequence of designing the workflow in this way?

060.en: Delivering outcomes more quickly and consistently

061.en: Ensuring employees always follow processes without question

062.en: Trying to provide a solution for every exception will often lead to over-complication. When creating a product or a practice, designers need to think about exceptions, but they cannot cover them all. Instead, they should design rules that can be used to handle exceptions generally. Ref 5.2.6

063.en: Why should organizations consider the interaction of ITIL Guiding Principles?

064.en: Because principles are interdependent and complement each other

065.en: Because one principle is always superior to the rest

066.en: Because principles must be applied in a strict order

067.en: Because one principle is usually suficient for any situation

068.en: In addition to being aware of the ITIL Guiding Principles, it is important to recognize that they interact with and depend upon each other. For example, if an organization is committed to progressing iteratively with feedback, it should also think and work holistically to ensure that each iteration of an improvement includes all the elements necessary to deliver real results. Similarly, making use of appropriate feedback is key to collaboration, and focusing on what will truly be valuable to the customer makes it easier to keep things simple and practical. Ref 5.2.8

069.en: What is the role of a governing body in an organization?

070.en: It is accountable for performance and compliance at the highest level

071.en: It is responsible for day-to-day operations

072.en: It manages the technical details of digital products directly

073.en: It focuses exclusively on financial reporting

074.en: “Every organization is directed by a governing body: a person or group of people who are accountable at the highest level for the performance and compliance of the organization.” Ref 5.3.1

075.en: Which of the following is NOT a success metric of ‘discover’ activity?

076.en: Strategic fit of the organization’s products and service offerings

077.en: Market relevance of the products and service offerings

078.en: Service performance against the agreed SLA targets

079.en: Stakeholder satisfaction with products and service offerings

080.en: “Service performance and user feedback records and reports” is part of the ‘Deliver’ activity. The key metrics of success of the ‘Discover’ activity are: “Strategic fit of the organization’s products and service offerings; market relevance of the products and service offerings; stakeholder satisfaction with products and service offerings; commercial success of the products (if applicable).” Ref 4.8.2, Table 4.7, 4.2.2, Table 4.1

082.en: A service that fully or largely relies on digital products

083.en: A combination of technology resources designed for consumers

084.en: The transfer of goods from provider to consumer

085.en: A catalogue of services for consumers

086.en: A digital service is “a service that fully or largely relies on digital products.” Ref 3.1.2

087.en: Which term describes “what an organization does for its consumers and other stakeholders and why”?

092.en: An organization’s purpose is “what an organization does for its consumers and other stakeholders and why.” Ref 5.4.1

093.en: Which statement BEST explains the relationship between an organization’s purpose and its operating model?

094.en: The operating model defines the organization’s financial strategy to achieve its purpose

095.en: The organization’s purpose determines why it exists, while the operating model shows how it fulfils that purpose

096.en: The operating model replaces the organization’s purpose once the value chain is defined

097.en: The purpose and operating model are unrelated because one focuses on customers and the other on internal processes

098.en: An operating model is “A conceptual and/or visual representation of how an organization co-creates value with its customers and other stakeholders, as well as how the organization runs itself.” Ref 5.4.1

099.en: Which of the following describes a management practice?

100.en: A series of steps that an organization uses to create and deliver products

101.en: A set of organizational resources and capabilities designed to perform work or accomplish an objective

102.en: A visual representation of how an organization co-creates value with stakeholders

103.en: A set of interconnected activities that an organization performs to create and deliver products

104.en: “Management practice” is “a set of organizational resources and capabilities designed and adopted for performing work or accomplishing an objective.” Ref 5.5

105.en: Which aspect of an Oficial ITIL Practice Guide describes the roles, competencies, and responsibilities needed for a specific practice?

108.en: The Organizations and people aspect of a practice guide describes “roles, competencies and responsibilities” as well as “organizational solutions and teams (specific to the practice)” Ref 5.5.1, Table 5.3

109.en: A company plans an improvement initiative and ensures it is clearly linked to organizational goals and objectives. Which continual improvement step is being performed?

113.en: Where do we want to be?

114.en: “Each improvement initiative should support the organization’s goals and objectives. The first step of the continual improvement model is to define the vision of the initiative. This provides context for all subsequent decisions and links individual actions to the organization’s vision for the future.” Ref 5.6.1.1

115.en: Which of the following is NOT one of the steps in value stream mapping?

122.en: A formal description of one or more services designed to address consumer needs

123.en: The access to the service provider’s resources and their use according to the agreed terms and conditions

124.en: A combination of an organization’s resources based on digital technology and designed to offer value to consumers

125.en: Actions performed by a service provider or jointly by a service provider and consumer

126.en: “Digital products are a combination of an organization’s resources based on digital technology and designed to offer value to consumers.” Ref 4.5.1

127.en: Which of the following is a key success metric for the ‘acquire’ activity?

128.en: Number and impact of incidents and performance deviations

129.en: Quality of the resources and services outsourced from suppliers

130.en: Negative impact of changes on service availability and performance

131.en: The key metrics of the ‘acquire’ activity are “Quality of the resources and services; acquire cycle time; adherence to the product roadmap and other relevant guidelines; stakeholder satisfaction with the ‘acquire’ activity, timelines, and acquired resources.” Ref 4.4.2, Table 4.3

132.en: Which BEST describes the relationship between digital services and digital products?

133.en: Digital products are always based on digital services

134.en: Digital services are always based on digital products

135.en: Digital services and digital products exist independently

136.en: Digital products are service actions performed by providers

137.en: “Digital services are always based on digital products. Products provide capabilities, while service offerings describe the potential value they offer to customers.” Ref 3.1.2

138.en: Which role takes responsibility for the outcomes of service consumption?

143.en: The “Customer” is the role that defines the requirements for products and services and takes responsibility for the outcomes of service consumption. Ref 3.2.1.1

144.en: Which type of service relationship typically focuses on support and eficiency through standardized services?

149.en: The “typical focus” of the ‘basic relationship’ is “support and eficiency”. Ref 3.2.2, Table 3.1

150.en: Which statement about the ‘band of visibility’ is CORRECT?

151.en: It includes only the activities visible to the service provider

152.en: It applies exclusively to modern, technology-based digital service models

153.en: It represents all aspects visible between provider and consumer organizations

154.en: It defines the complete path of the customer’s service journey

155.en: The “band of visibility” is the sum of the aspects of the service consumer organizations visible to the service provider, and the aspects of the service provider organizations visible to the service consumer. Ref 3.2.3, Figure 3.4

156.en: What is the MAIN purpose of the ‘discover’ activity?

157.en: To develop and test digital products

158.en: To secure and allocate resources eficiently

159.en: To align product capabilities with consumer needs and strategy

160.en: To maintain and monitor digital products

161.en: The main purpose of the ‘discover’ activity “is to ensure continual alignment of the product roadmaps and related service offerings with the needs of service consumers and with the organizational strategy.” Ref 4.2.1

162.en: Which lifecycle activity is focused on creating prototypes and specifications?

167.en: “The purpose of the ‘design’ activity is to create prototypes and specifications for products and services, detailing their functionality, user experience, and operational framework.” Ref 4.3.1

168.en: What is the PRIMARY purpose of the ‘acquire’ activity?

169.en: Resolve incidents and fulfil recovery procedures

170.en: Secure and allocate necessary resources eficiently
